title: Jonesy, Ellington's valet
summary: Bigard tells of Jonesy's devotion and how Ellington's circle hid him from his dying wife.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Retribution always gets you in the end, you know? Jonesy -- Jonesy was so devoted to Duke. And Duke used to keep that man out all night in -- to be with him, to guard him because he -- he always feel that somebody's going to beat him up or something. And he wanted Jonesy around him to help him out. And, when Jonesy was dying, I remember this -- [anyway] out here, California, and his wife couldn't see him, they hid Jonesy from his wife and his wife had to go and get a lawyer and she was -- used to work for the biggest one around here, that -- what's that big lawyer around here, a real biggy, well I'll get it anyway, so they finally told -- send one of his representatives where Duke was staying, said if they don't produce Jonesy within so many hours, they was going to come and get him. And that's the only time his wife got to see Jonesy and she took him to her home.
How many years was he with you, from 1927 to when?
Oh, God, till the end. Till the end of his.
Which was when? I don't know.
I don't know when Jonesy died -- I haven't -- you -- you have any idea? No it's --
I saw references to him in 1938, in Ulanov's book and after that I don't know -- I never knew him.

Well he was -- that was probably about that time, anyway, but and he was with Duke night and day, Duke kept that man up all hours. But that's the only time she got to see her husband. They was hiding the man. And Bea was one of the main instigators of that thing. Bea, Duke's woman or whatever you want to call her. And he was -- he was - see when he -- something happened years ago between he and his wife and he's been terrible with the -- with women ever since, I mean like he's always trying to make somebody's wife, because somebody made his wife and he -- they got in such a fight, that slash he has on the side of his face, she cut him while he was sleeping. With a razor.
Bea said once that he could not stand to see a man and a woman happy together.

Yeah, he probably couldn't. Unless he could make trouble for them and in any way he could, he could do it and that's why he was afraid, because somebody threatened him. I think a couple of guys threatened him one time.
